Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the AetherMed Devices Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Elena Vasquez, CEO; Michael Chen, CFO; Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Lisa Moreno, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. AetherMed Devices achieved record results this quarter, reflecting the strength of our diversified portfolio and our commitment to innovation.

Today, I will cover eight key aspects of our performance:
1. FDA approvals and CE marks obtained
2. Organic revenue growth by segment and geography
3. New product launches and contribution to growth
4. Capital equipment vs consumables mix trends
5. Revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year
6. Key assumptions underlying the guidance
7. SG&A expense management and efficiency gains
8. Procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary

Michael will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Raj will update us on our technology advancements, and Lisa will discuss our market strategies. We'll then conclude with a Q&A session.

Now, let's get started with FDA approvals and CE marks obtained.

I'm particularly proud of our regulatory momentum this quarter, which has been instrumental in driving our 28% year-over-year revenue growth in the Medical Devices segment. Regulatory progress isn't just about checking boxes—it's our strategic edge in a field where these hurdles block most competitors. In Q3, we secured four key FDA approvals and clearances, pushing our trailing 12-month total to 12—a 50% jump from last year, far exceeding the industry average of 8-10 for peers like iRhythm or Shockwave Medical.

Leading the pack is the PMA approval for our AetherValve TR, our next-gen transcatheter aortic valve replacement system for low-risk patients with severe aortic stenosis. This follows our Q1 2023 IDE approval and the ASPIRE trial, enrolling 850 patients at 45 U.S. sites, with a 95% procedural success rate and 1.2% 30-day all-cause mortality—outperforming Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien 3 Ultra RESILIA by 15% on composite endpoints.

We also gained 510(k) clearance for three innovations: the AetherStent Neo, a bioresorbable drug-eluting stent using our sirolimus-eluting polymer that cuts late lumen loss by 22% compared to Boston Scientific's Synergy XD in bench tests; the EchoGuide Pro, an AI-powered intravascular ultrasound catheter for real-time 3D imaging and automated plaque analysis; and the RhythmSync ICD lead with fractal coil design reducing dislodgement risks by 35%, per our SIGNAL post-market study.

This stems from our Regulatory Accelerator Program, launched in 2022, trimming average FDA review to 7.2 months for 510(k)s and 18 months for PMAs—25% better year-over-year and 30% ahead of FDA FY2023 medians. We've held 22 pre-submission meetings this year, used Q-Submissions for real-world evidence alignment, and employed digital twin modeling with Siemens Healthineers' Simcenter for over 10,000 virtual implantations, speeding bench-to-IDE by 40%.

On CE marks, we've tackled the tough EU MDR environment—where approvals fell 40% industry-wide since 2021—and earned six Class III marks in Q3, including full certification for AetherValve TR and AetherStent Neo. This opens EuroZone commercialization in a structural heart market growing 16% CAGR to $4.2 billion by 2028, per Evaluate MedTech. Our timelines averaged 14 months versus peers' 24-month delays at Notified Bodies like those hitting Medtronic. We're chasing UKCA via MHRA's mutual recognition with FDA data and have filed three NMPA submissions in China for AetherStent Neo, aiming for mid-2025 in a 12% CAGR stent market.

In the U.S., these unlock $225 million in FY2025 incremental revenue at 75% gross margins—60% from new ramps, 40% from label expansions for outpatient TAVR under CMS code C1832. Europe bolsters our 8% drug-eluting stent share, up from 5%, challenging Abbott's Xience amid polymer issues in ESC data. APAC is next, with post-CE distributor partnerships in Japan for PMDA, targeting $50 million TAM in high-bleed patients.

These de-risk our $1.2 billion pipeline—70% Class III—and prove our Regulate-to-Innovate approach, with 92% first-cycle approvals versus industry's 65%. AetherValve TR's 22Fr profile and 10% lower CPP position us for 5-7% TAVR share gain in year one, like Shockwave in IVL. Ahead, eight more FDA actions in Q4, including Breakthrough Designation for PulseNeuro HF renal denervation in a $3 billion heart failure market. We've budgeted $45 million for RAP in FY2025, leveraging our TRIDENT registry of 5,000 patients for post-market claims.

Now, let's talk about organic revenue growth by segment and geography.

Excluding our NeuroPulse acquisition and FX headwinds, we posted 9.4% organic growth year-over-year, up from 7.2% in Q2 and beating our 8-9% guide. This highlights our core strength amid elective rebounds and adjacency investments.

By segment, Cardiovascular—42% of revenue—led with 12.8% organic growth, from 15% TAVR volumes on AetherFlow Gen3 gaining 220 bps U.S. share to 28% per Milliman, plus 1% pricing despite Medicare NTAP pressures. SealGuard XL LAA closure added $18 million early U.S. sales.

Orthopaedics (25%) grew 6.2%, matching hip/knee recovery to 92% pre-COVID per Definitive Healthcare. Triad Porous Acetabular Cup drove 9% procedures, integrated with AetherBot robotics in 45% top U.S. accounts. Trauma softened on ASPs, but digital templating lifted volumes 20%.

MedSurg (18%) rose 8.1%, led by single-use endoscopes and EndoShield staplers up 14% in EMEA bariatrics vs. Ethicon. PulseWave SCS neuromodulation added $22 million, with 2.5x ROI from U.S. reps.

Diabetes (7.9%) and Vision (5.6%) followed, with GlucoSync 2.0 pump up 11% integrating Dexcom G7, and femtosecond lasers offsetting lens weakness.

Geographically, U.S. (68%) grew 7.9% organically despite 2% Medicare drag, beating Medtronic's 6% CV and Stryker's 5% ortho via 300+ clinical specialists in IDNs.

EMEA (18%) surged 13.2% organic on 16% Germany/UK from CE expansions and France LPPR; Poland localization cut leads 25% for NHS backlogs.

Asia-Pacific (22%) hit 14.7%, China 18% on NRD TAVR coverage in 85% Tier-1 hospitals, Japan 12% with Terumo robotics, India 25% ortho kits.

Rest of World 9.1%, Latin America 11% on endoscopy tenders.

This validates Precision Growth: 60% volumes, 25% high-acuity mix, 15% pricing. $150 million R&D in AI AetherHub boosted efficiency 18%. Q4 organic 9-11%, FY 9%, for 8-10% CAGR to 2026 on 105 million procedures per IQVIA.

Moving on to new product launches and contribution to growth.

New products drove 28% year-over-year growth, now 22% of revenue up from 15%, capturing procedural booms, CMS OPPS tailwinds, and precision shifts.

Cardiology flagship: EvoFlow TAVR launched February, with nitinol frame and leak skirt hitting 98% success in ORBIT-3 trial vs. 95% benchmark. Q3 U.S. volumes topped 4,500 cases, +150% sequential, $185 million sales—65% new cardio revenue, 320 bps company growth. ASPs $32,000 with NTAP.

NeuroStim DBS post-June PMA: AI leads cut programming 40%, 12-year battery; $92 million Q3, +75% Y/Y, expanding early Parkinson's market.

Ortho robotics: ApexFlex knee system, EMEA Q1/U.S. August 510(k), modular haptics reduce damage 25% per FLEX-NAV. 120 installs YTD, $68 million capital/recurring at 55% disposable attach $2,200/case, 18 cases/system/month, 42% procedures, 180 bps growth.

U.S. (58% new sales) +2.2 TAVR share to 14%; Europe (25%) 35% on tenders; APAC 52% Y/Y Japan/China; EM $22 million +90%.

$1.2 billion R&D (12% sales) on digital/sustainability/M&A like $450 million NeuroVance. 2025 pipeline: CardioSense AFib wearable, bioresorbable stents. New products 30-35% growth FY25 on 4.5% TAM CAGR.

Next, capital equipment vs consumables mix trends.

Our mix shifted to 32% capital, 68% consumables—up from 35/65 prior year—bolstering annuity streams at 70%+ EBITDA. Consumables $285 million +14% constant currency on 9% volumes, 112% attach.

Capital $142 million +4% YoY, flat sequential amid CapEx squeezes per Vizient/Kaiser 15-20% pullbacks. Book-to-bill 1.15x.

Over eight quarters, consumables from 62% to 68%, 16% CAGR vs. 7% capital. Drivers: AI Precision Suite +22% efficiency, 2.3 kits endoscopy; single-use stents/catheters +22% at 28% consumables; service utilization 78% +19% revenue.

U.S. (52%) consumables 72% on ASC shift; Europe (28%) 64% +8%; APAC (20%) 71% +21%.

Consumables 75-80% margins vs. capital 45-50%; targeting 70/30 by 2026 with $450 million R&D on interoperability/digital twins +5-7% attach. Positions for 12-15% FY24 growth.

Then, revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year.

For Q4, revenue $685-695 million, 9-11% reported/10-12% organic. Structural heart mid-teens on TAVR/AetherValve TR ramps >150 U.S. accounts. EP low double-digits on RhythmSync AI. Lapping pacemaker comps.

Americas 65% growth, U.S. 12-14%; EMEA 7-9%; APAC flat-3% China NDRC.

Adjusted gross 68-69% +150 bps on mix/Galway ramp/FX; op 24-25%; FCF >90%.

FY2025: $2.85-2.95 billion, 11-15% reported/12-16% organic. Structural heart 16-18%, EP 13-15%, legacy flat-3%. Americas 14-16%, EMEA 10-12%, APAC 6-8%.

Gross 69-70%, op 25-27%, EPS $4.85-5.15 +14%. Risks: CMS ASPs, inflation; tailwinds: CardiClip TR H1, Holter Q2.

Then, key assumptions underlying the guidance.

Guidance: FY24 revenue $5.25-5.40 billion 8-11% reported/7-10% organic; EPS $4.85-5.05 +9-14%; gross 68.5-69.5%; op 24.5-25.5% +100-150 bps.

Revenue: mid-single volumes +12% Q2 accel; ASPs 2-3% premium; 1-2% FX. Structural heart 10-12% 15% TAVR; neuro/EP 8-10% 12% DBS; robotics 6-8% 60% disposables. <1% inorganic.

Regions: U.S. 8-10%; EMEA 6-8%; APAC 11-13% China 18%.

Margins: gross +200 bps Singapore 95% yield, costs down; OpEx +7% R&D 12-12.5% $650-675 million Phase III DBS/robotics; SG&A 28%; interest $120 million; tax 18-19%.

Pillars: 5-7% procedure CAGR IQVIA; $1.2 billion pipeline 70% approval; non-China 40%. Macro: 5% U.S. spend, stable reimb.

Then, SG&A expense management and efficiency gains.

Q3 SG&A $285 million +4% on 12% revenue, 28.2% ratio -280 bps lowest in 3 years; H1 28.7% -350 bps, $65 million savings.

Efficiency 2.0: Sales (55%) flat $157 million despite 15% volumes; reps -8% to 2,260; Virtual OR AI/VR cut travel 25% $12 million, 85% adoption, EMEA +18%.

G&A -7% $84 million RPA UiPath 40% processes $18 million savings 300% ROI; Bangalore procurement 12-15% discounts; headcount -10%.

Admin -11% $44 million outsourcing Genpact; China hub -22%; vacated U.S. sites $8 million save.

U.S. -320 bps Medicare offset; EMEA -250 bps; APAC flat.

FY24 target 27-28%, 2025 +100-200 bps robotics/digital. AI CRM +22% productivity; $0.28 Q3 EPS add, to 18-20% margins 2026.

Finally, procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary.

Procedures +14% YoY +6% sequential, 5th double-digit quarter vs. 8-10% industry.

Cardio (45%) +18%: coronary +22% AetherStent 28% share; TAVR +32% 150k EvoCore; structural +25%; ICD/CRT +12%.

Ortho/spine (25%) +11%: hip/knee +15% >2019 Triad; spine +9% Viper; robotics 2x.

Endo/neuro (20%) +10/13%: VizScope +25% ERCP; NeuroVive +19%.

Neuro/other +9% sacral +16%.

U.S. (55%) +17% 102% 2019 ASC 28%; Europe (25%) +10% 98% Germany/UK; China/APAC (12%) +25% 120% 2019; ROW +12%.

Recovery 105% global 2019; headwinds staffing/inflation/pricing. Initiatives: POP AI +15% throughput; FlexiGuide/Q4 launches; reps +18%.

Q4 13-15%, FY24 14%; 10-12% decade growth demographics/VBC.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen for a review of our financial results.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Elena. As Elena outlined so comprehensively, we delivered exceptional financial performance this quarter, with revenue hitting records across segments and margins expanding on mix and efficiencies. Total Q3 revenue reached $670 million, up 28% reported and 22% organic, driven by the regulatory wins, volume surges, and new launches Elena detailed. Gross margins hit 67.5%, up 200 basis points year-over-year on high-margin TAVR and consumables shifts. Adjusted operating income was $165 million, with EPS of $1.12, +22%. Expenses controlled tightly, as we'll touch on. Balance sheet strong with $1.2 billion cash, supporting buybacks and R&D.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Raj Patel for an update on our product pipeline.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Michael. We are excited about the progress we are making in our technology roadmap. Our latest innovation, PulseNeuro HF, our neuromodulation platform for renal denervation targeting heart failure reduction, is poised to transform the $3 billion market with superior efficacy in real-world data. We expect FDA approval in Q1 2025.

Building on Elena's new launch highlights, our R&D pipeline remains robust at $1.2 billion committed, 12% of sales. We're advancing AI integrations across platforms, like EchoGuide Pro expansions and digital twins accelerating trials by 40%. Phase III readouts for bioresorbable stents and haptic robotics in Q4 position us for 16-18% structural heart growth. Sustainability focus with 30% waste reduction in new devices. Next up: CardioSense wearable for $15 billion digital diagnostics.

Next, Lisa Moreno with some insights on our commercial strategy.

Lisa Moreno:
Thank you, Raj. We are focused on driving commercial excellence and expanding our global reach. Our strategic partnerships are enabling us to access new markets and customer segments.

Leveraging Q3 wins, U.S. sales force at 450 reps gained 220 bps TAVR share via IDN embeds and ASC bundles. EMEA tenders in Germany/UK/NHS drove 13% growth; APAC partnerships with Terumo/local distributors ramp China NRD/Japan PMDA/India camps. Value-based contracts with UnitedHealth/Payers secure 15% volumes. Digital tools like Virtual OR/AetherHub boost productivity 22%, targeting 70/30 consumables mix. Emerging markets via Zimmer-like models add $22 million EM.

Now, back to Elena for Q&A.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Lisa. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star then one. Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee - Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Elena, on the FDA approvals, particularly AetherValve TR—how do you see the share gains materializing given Edwards' dominance, and any update on the eight Q4 actions?

Elena Vasquez:
Great question, David. With AetherValve TR's smaller 22Fr profile and lower CPP, we're positioned like Shockwave did in IVL—peeling 5-7% U.S. TAVR share in year one from low-risk ramps. ASPIRE data superiority drives adoption; 150+ accounts live already. On Q4, PulseNeuro HF Breakthrough is key for heart failure pivot, plus three 510(k)s; 92% first-cycle rate holds via RAP and TRIDENT RWE.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with J.P. Morgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen - J.P. Morgan:
Thanks. Michael, your FY25 guidance looks strong at 12-16% organic—can you unpack the key assumptions around APAC stabilization and margin drivers?

Michael Chen:
Absolutely, Emily. Assumptions embed China NDRC stabilization post-stents, with TAVR/neuro NMPA adding 6-8% APAC; Japan/India tailwinds. Margins to 69-70% gross on Galway scale, robotics mix 75%+; op 25-27% as SG&A leverages to 27-28%, R&D steady 13-14%. Volumes mid-single global, ASPs 2-3%, FX neutral. Upside from CardiClip TR $5B TAM H1.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Robert Kim - Morgan Stanley:
Hi team. Lisa, commercial thoughts on EMEA softness in capital and how partnerships accelerate robotics attach in APAC?

Lisa Moreno:
Thanks, Robert. EMEA capital lagged on NHS/DRG but rebounding 25% Q3 orders post-CE NeuroGuide; bundles stabilize ASPs. APAC robotics ApexFlex China clearance early, Terumo Japan driving 52% new product growth; 55% attach ramping to 18 cases/system. Localized manufacturing Suzhou cuts leads 30%, high-volume focus yields 2.5x ROI.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Patel with Leerink Partners. Please go ahead.

Sarah Patel - Leerink Partners:
Congrats. Raj, on procedure trends—any color on Q4 outlook amid staffing headwinds, and how POP platform scales?

Raj Patel:
Thanks, Sarah. Q4 volumes 13-15% on U.S. ASC 28% penetration, China 120% 2019. Staffing caps 90-95% OR but POP AI scheduling +15% throughput, 22% same-day TAVR discharges. Utilization 85-92%; FlexiGuide PCI adds 50k procedures annually. Confident in 14% FY24.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for your thoughtful questions. We remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver sustainable growth.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
